_readme: Hand-written editorial notes for the home page's 'This week at the W3C' section. Newest first. The page shows the newest note whose date falls inside the current activity window (public/data/wcag3-recent-activity.json), so a note disappears on its own once the window moves past it. Keep each point checkable against a linked issue or pull request.

notes.headline: The draft text barely moved; the issue tracker did.

points.text: A coordinated cleanup of the word “programmatically”: about a dozen issues and pull requests propose moving provisions such as Change of content notified, Preselections visible, Relationships detectable and Errors associated onto formally defined terms (“programmatically determinable”, “programmatically detectable”).

A proposed new scoping statement would describe WCAG 3 as covering “user facing digital content”, name AI-generated content explicitly, and say 3.0 focuses on web content and is not yet complete for software and documents.
The definition of decorative images drew 34 comments in its first week, alongside a new issue arguing decorative images should not have to be “programmatically hidden”.
Two conformance proposals are open: removing the dependency on conformance claims, and rewriting the Explainer's conformance section.
The only change merged into the editor's draft was editorial: the Explainer's glossary definitions were tidied. No provision or conformance text changed.
